paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption_used: The effect of context masking on case tasks grouped by language family, with error bars indicating standard deviation. Six model configurations are compared across nine language families: mBERT-L2, XLM-L2, mBERT-R2, XLM-R2, mBERT-B2, and XLM-B2. The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with most configurations reaching between 17 and 25, while Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models. Notably, IE-Germanic exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations, with XLM-B2 reaching approximately 20 in IE-Germanic. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, suggesting high variability, and the mBERT-L2 bars in Semitic reach approximately 15. In IE-Slavic, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) dominate over the L2 and R2 variants, with effects approximately twice as large.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking on case tasks, grouped by language family, with error bars representing standard deviation. The horizontal axis displays nine language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged in that order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled "effect," is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. For each language family, six model configurations are represented as grouped bars: mBERT-L2 (light blue), XLM-L2 (dark blue), mBERT-R2 (light green), XLM-R2 (dark green), mBERT-B2 (light red), and XLM-B2 (dark red). The IE-Indic family shows the largest effects overall, with bars reaching approximately 20–25 for most configurations, particularly mBERT-R2 (around 20) and XLM-R2 (around 18), while XLM-B2 is near 21. In contrast, the Uralic and Isolate families show near-zero effects across all models, with bars clustered near 0. The IE-Germanic family exhibits consistently higher effects than IE-Romance across all configurations; for example, XLM-B2 reaches approximately 20 in IE-Germanic, whereas in IE-Romance, the same model shows an effect of about 6. The Semitic family displays the widest error bars overall, indicating high variability, with mBERT-L2 reaching approximately 15. In the IE-Slavic family, the B2 variants (mBERT-B2 and XLM-B2) show the largest effects, approximately 17 and 16 respectively, which are roughly twice as large as the L2 and R2 variants (around 8–9). Bars are not sorted by height within each group, and no specific bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding.
